findings.text: Fractional divider provider pairs a generic hardware anchor with a register reference, independent placement descriptors for two bitfields, a small option byte, an optional approximation callback that refines desired versus parent rates into field values, and a shared protection reference.
Fractional divider zero based encoding uses bit zero, big endian access uses bit one, and power of two presentation uses bit two.
Multiplier provider combines a generic hardware anchor with a register reference, placement descriptor for one bitfield, a small option byte, and a shared protection reference.
Multiplier zero bypass uses bit zero, closest rounding uses bit one, and big endian access uses bit two.
Composite provider aggregates a generic hardware anchor with a local operation table plus separate subordinate hardware anchors and operation tables for selection, rate control, and gating roles.
Each provider type offers a conversion from its embedded generic hardware anchor back to the enclosing provider object, preserving identity between outer descriptor and inner anchor.

Hardware accessor helpers expose reinterpretation between opaque clock handle and hardware anchor, propagation of clock and core associations from one anchor to another, and a predicate testing whether rate changes may propagate to the parent.
Cell tables for firmware clock lookup provide either a counted array of opaque clock handles or a counted flexible array of hardware anchors with compiler assisted bound annotation.

Firmware clock registration helpers declare probe callbacks tied to compatibility strings, marking the firmware node initialized or clearing its populated marker before invoking the provider callback.

Initialization descriptor builders supply named clock setup with operation table and flags while varying parent linkage by name string, hardware anchor, firmware name, or arrays thereof, including a parentless variant and single parent convenience forms.

Fixed factor descriptor builders instantiate divider multiplier objects whose initialization points at shared fixed factor operations with caller supplied name, parent linkage, factors, and flags across name, hardware, array, and firmware naming styles.
In the routed configuration provider registration and parent helpers are neutral shims reporting success while lookup helpers report a missing entry error, indicating clock firmware support disabled.

Clock notification state comprises a registry entry linking a clock with a sleepable notification chain and list linkage, a transition record carrying old and new rates, and a bulk acquisition record pairing an identifier with a clock handle.
Pre change indication uses bit zero, post change uses bit one, and aborted change uses bit two.

In the routed configuration notification registration, accuracy, phase, and duty cycle mutators report unsupported operation, scaled duty query yields zero, and clock identity comparison reduces to pointer equality.
Rate exclusivity acquisition reports success with a no operation release, and context save reports success with a no operation restore, indicating no persistent state in this configuration.
Fractional divider and multiplier providers do not embed protection but hold a pointer to an external lock, requiring callers to provide shared exclusion covering register updates where needed.
Preparation and bulk preparation paths may sleep and must not be used in non sleepable context, with two build dependent sleep annotation forms both permitting rescheduling.
Bulk unprepare mirrors sleepable teardown and the enabled when prepared query yields false in this configuration.
Clock acquisition helpers in this configuration either return an empty handle for single lookups or report success for bulk operations without populating hardware backed state.

Enable, rate, range, and parent helpers in this configuration report neutral success or zero or true or empty outcomes with no observable hardware effect, including put and disable shims that perform no action.

Combined helpers establish preparation before activation and unwind preparation when activation fails, while teardown helpers reverse that order, with bulk forms applying the same ordering across arrays and range clearing expanding to full span.
Optional single lookup maps a missing firmware entry to an empty result while preserving other outcomes, and firmware indexed or named lookups report a missing entry error in this configuration.

Closure machinery centers on a waitlist head for lockless chaining and a closure object with two views sharing storage, one exposing queue, synchronizer, linkage, and continuation, the other exposing generic work, plus parent linkage, atomic reference state, acquisition marker, and optional debug annotation.

Closure reference word reserves a low counter field with high flag bits marking destructor ownership, waiting membership, and running execution, with derived masks isolating guard transitions, counter value, and an initial running count of one.
Closure destructor flag uses bit twenty six, waiting flag uses bit twenty eight, running flag uses bit thirty, counter occupies lower twenty six bits, and guard mask shifts combined flags by one.
Debug tags use dead value c054dead hex, live heap value c054a11e hex, and live stack value c05451cc hex.

Remaining count query masks the atomic state to its counter field, while synchronous wait helpers delegate to external blocking primitives only when a prior acquisition was recorded, otherwise completing immediately with success.
Debug creation, destruction, and instruction tracking helpers are no operation unless debug support is enabled, while the stopped transition clears the running mark from the shared reference word.

Continuation installation records the callback and target queue with debug tracking, and dispatch either enqueues generic work when a queue is present or invokes the continuation inline, guarded by a build time check that continuation and work entry share placement.

Acquisition marks that blocking may be required and raises the shared count, conditional acquisition succeeds only when the counter is nonzero using an acquire ordered compare exchange loop, and initialization establishes a running count of one with optional parent linkage and zeroed stack forms.

Clock usage follows a two stage lifecycle where preparation must precede activation and bulk forms preserve all or nothing ordering, with notification phases bracketing rate transitions and abort handling.

Enqueue failure triggers a fatal trap, debug builds trap on unexpected remaining counts during synchronous wait and on reference misuse, and inline dispatch executes in caller context so blocking or long work risks stalling the invoker.

Closure objects carry no internal spin protection in the fragments, exclusion relies on atomic reference updates and workqueue ownership with waiting membership owned by the holder and cleared by the waker.
Both clock and closure headers employ include guards to ensure single inclusion within a translation unit.
